title: MockLLM: A Multi-Agent Behavior Collaboration Framework for Online Job Seeking and Recruiting

problem.claim: Online recruitment requires applications that improve person-job matching.

gap.claim: Traditional resume and job-description text analysis does not adequately capture the dynamic and interactive aspects of recruitment.

contributions.claim: MockLLM generates and evaluates mock interview interactions through mock interview generation and two-sided evaluation using a handshake protocol.
MockLLM simulates interviewer and candidate roles to support consistent, collaborative, real-time, two-sided matching.
MockLLM uses reflection memory generation and dynamic strategy modification to refine behavior from previous experience.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MockLLM as a novel framework for generating and evaluating mock interview interactions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating MockLLM on real-world data from Boss Zhipin.
The authors report that MockLLM outperforms existing methods in matching accuracy, scalability, and adaptability across job domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online recruitment has increased demand for improved person-job matching.
Text-based traditional methods are limited in representing dynamic and interactive recruitment.
LLMs offer role-based adaptive dialogue simulation relevant to recruitment.
MockLLM combines mock interview generation, two-sided handshake evaluation, role simulation, reflection memory, and dynamic strategy modification.
The framework is evaluated on Boss Zhipin data, with reported gains across matching accuracy, scalability, and cross-domain adaptability.

source_observation.claim: The framework models both sides of a recruitment interaction and uses prior interaction experience to modify strategies.

interpretation.claim: Two-sided role simulation combined with experience-based adaptation may better represent interactive matching than static text analysis.

application.claim: Interactive matching systems could benefit from explicit role modeling, reciprocal evaluation, memory, and dynamic strategy updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported recruitment setting or Boss Zhipin data.

unknowns: No dataset size, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are provided.
No implementation details or ablation results are provided.
No limitations or generalization analysis is provided.
